'''Peng Jiamu''' ({{CJKV|s=彭加木|p=Péng Jiāmù}}, born 19 May 1925, disappeared 17 June 1980) was a Chinese biochemist and explorer.

==Biography==
Peng was born in [[Guangzhou]], [[Guangdong]] province, in 1935.<ref name=PDaily>{{cite web|title=Memories of great desert explorer live on|url=http://english.peopledaily.com.cn/200604/19/text20060419_259463.html|website=People's Daily Online|publisher=People's Daily|accessdate=8 September 2015}}</ref> He received a biology degree from Central University of China (now [[Nanjing University]]), graduating in 1947 and subsequently joined the [[Shanghai Institute of Biochemistry]], where he studied and worked under [[Cao Tianqin]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang|first=Youshang |authorlink=Zhang Youshang |date=June 2010|title=In memory of Professor Tianqin Cao (Tien-chin Tsao) |journal=Protein & Cell|volume=1|issue=6|pages=507–509|issn=1674-8018|pmc=4875321|pmid=21246905|doi=10.1007/s13238-010-0074-2 }}</ref> He joined several scientific expeditions to [[Xinjiang]] organized by the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS), starting in 1956. On the expeditions, he catalogued species of flora and fauna and measured potassium accumulation in the [[Lop Nor]] desert.

In 1979, a year before he disappeared in the Lop Desert, he was promoted to the Vice President of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. "Science," he said, "is to walk a road not travelled by other people."<ref name=Explorer>{{cite web|title=Disappearance of Peng Jiamu|url=https://explorersweb.com/exploration-mysteries-the-disappearance-of-peng-jiamu/}}</ref>

==Disappearance==
During the year 1980, Peng would lead an expedition to the Lop Nur desert, where he would disappear on 17 June a few days after a dispute, leaving a note referencing that he had gone out to find water.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boissoneault |first=Lorraine |date=2016-01-28 |title=3 Explorers Who Vanished Without a Trace |url=https://daily.jstor.org/3-explorers-who-vanished-without-a-trace/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=JSTOR Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

Peng's disappearance had been during the cold war, and it would be the subject of many conspiracy theories that have been proposed to explain his disappearance, from that of the [[Pisces Jade Pendant|Pisces Jade Pendant theory]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Feng |first=Qing |date=2025-02-15 |title=The Enigmatic Jade Pendant: Unraveling the Mystery of China's "Double Fish" Legend |url=https://pandayoo.com/post/the-enigmatic-jade-pendant-unraveling-the-mystery-of-chinas-double-fish-legend/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=PandaYoo |language=en-US}}</ref> defection to or abductions by foreign powers,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Abreu |first=Kristine De |date=2020-10-30 |title=Exploration Mysteries: The Disappearance of Peng Jiamu » Explorersweb |url=https://explorersweb.com/exploration-mysteries-the-disappearance-of-peng-jiamu/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=Explorersweb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Report says missing China scientist seen in U.S. - UPI Archives |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1980/10/11/Report-says-missing-China-scientist-seen-in-US/4844340084800/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=UPI |language=en}}</ref> the plant virus theory<ref>{{Cite web |last=laitimes |date=2021-10-26 |title=The most famous unsolved case after the founding of the People's Republic of China, Peng Jia Mu mysterious disappearance in Lop Nur, what happened in the end what Peng Jia Mu contributed to the country in his life The mysterious Peng Jia Mu disappeared looking for Peng Jia Mu Peng Jia Mu Missing version |url=http://www.laitimes.com/en/article/skq_sn0.html |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=laitimes |language=en}}</ref>, or extraterrestrial abductions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunwick |first=Robert Foyle |date=2018-06-06 |title=China Unsolved: A Scientist Vanishes |url=https://thechinaproject.com/2018/06/06/china-unsolved-a-scientist-vanishes/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=The China Project |language=en-US}}</ref>

A large-scale hunt for him was unsuccessful and widely covered by Chinese media. A TV documentary series named ''Searching for Peng Jiamu'' covered the events up to and after his disappearance.<ref>{{cite web|title=In Search of Peng Jiamu|url=http://english.cntv.cn/program/documentary/20130323/100652.shtml|website=CCTV.com English|publisher=China Central Television|accessdate=27 September 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304111631/http://english.cntv.cn/program/documentary/20130323/100652.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> On six occasions between 2005 and 2007, human remains were discovered that could have been his, but could not be proven as such. After the fourth hunt, he had been declared a revolutionary martyr by the party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunwick |first=Robert Foyle |date=2018-06-06 |title=China Unsolved: A Scientist Vanishes |url=https://thechinaproject.com/2018/06/06/china-unsolved-a-scientist-vanishes/ |access-date=2025-12-20 |website=The China Project |language=en-US}}</ref>
